reasoning: According to data from the Congressional Research Service (CRS), the Pew Research Center, and the Peter G. Peterson Foundation, the U.S. Congress has not passed all of its regular, individual annual appropriations bills on time (before the start of the new fiscal year on October 1) since Fiscal Year 1997. For FY 1997, the final appropriations bills were signed into law on September 30, 1996. Since then, Congress has consistently relied on continuing resolutions (CRs), omnibus spending packages, or late-season agreements passed well after the October 1 deadline to keep the federal government funded, making the statement historically accurate.
title: US Congress passed no budget on time since 1997
